hypothesis.title: productCatalogFailure feature flag enabled in flagd-config, injecting errors
hypothesis.summary: The productCatalogFailure feature flag was changed from 'off' to 'on' in the flagd-config ConfigMap 12 minutes before the alert. This caused product-catalog to start throwing "Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled" errors on ~10% of requests. These errors propagate upstream to frontend (directly and via recommendation/checkout), causing the frontend 5xx alert to fire.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend 5xx errors spiking from 0.4% to 10.5%. Traces show that 95% of failing frontend traces end in product-catalog, and 100% of failing product-catalog traces fail within product-catalog itself. The error message is consistent across all failures: "Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled (product OLJCESPC7Z)". The configmap/flagd-config shows productCatalogFailure was changed from 'off' to 'on' 12 minutes before the alert, which matches exactly when the errors started appearing in logs (first seen -12.0m). Product-catalog's own error rate jumped from 0.4% to 9.5% at the same time. The fraud-detection deployment 29 minutes before the alert is a red herring—fraud-detection is not on the call path from frontend to product-catalog, and the timing doesn't match the error spike. The valkey-cart restart is also unrelated—it's not on the failing traces. This is a clear config_change root cause in product-catalog: a feature flag was deliberately enabled to inject failures.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: ConfigMap flagd-config changed productCatalogFailure from 'off' to 'on' exactly 12 minutes before the alert, matching the timing of the error spike.
2,995 ERROR logs in product-catalog with the exact message 'Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', first seen 12 minutes ago, confirming the flag is active and causing failures.
100% of failing product-catalog traces terminate in product-catalog itself with the feature-flag error, proving this is the origin, not a downstream dependency.
95% of failing frontend traces end in product-catalog, showing the error propagates upstream from product-catalog to the alerting service.
Product-catalog error rate jumped from 0.4% to 9.5% starting 10 minutes before the alert, matching the config change timing and magnitude.
1,982 frontend errors calling product-catalog with the same feature-flag message, confirming the error propagation path from product-catalog to frontend.

suggested_actions.title: Revert the productCatalogFailure feature flag to 'off'
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo get cm flagd-config -o json | jq '.data["demo.flagd.json"] | fromjson | .flags.productCatalogFailure.state = "DISABLED"' | kubectl -n otel-demo patch cm flagd-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"demo.flagd.json":"$(cat -)"}}' && kubectl -n otel-demo rollout restart deployment/flagd
suggested_actions.rationale: Disabling the failure-injection flag will immediately stop the synthetic errors. This is the safest and most direct mitigation.

suggested_actions.title: Manually edit the flagd-config ConfigMap to set productCatalogFailure to 'off'
suggested_actions.rationale: If the automated patch fails, manually edit the ConfigMap and change productCatalogFailure state from 'on' to 'off', then restart flagd pods to pick up the change.

suggested_actions.title: Verify error rate drops after flag revert
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo logs -l app=product-catalog --tail=50 --since=2m | grep -i 'feature flag'
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm that product-catalog stops logging the feature-flag error message after the ConfigMap change propagates.

alternatives.why_less_likely: fraud-detection rolled out 2.0.2 → 2.0.3 29 minutes before the alert, but it is not on the call path from frontend to product-catalog (it only consumes from kafka asynchronously). The error spike started 12 minutes ago, not 29 minutes ago, and the error messages explicitly reference the productCatalogFailure flag, not fraud-detection.
